question: In intravascular haemolysis, serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) is elevated, serum haptoglobin is reduced, and the direct antiglobulin test (DAT/Coombs) is positive in autoimmune haemolytic anaemia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: In haemolysis: LDH rises (RBC enzyme leak), haptoglobin falls (consumed binding free Hb), unconjugated bilirubin rises, and reticulocytes increase. DAT is positive only in immune-mediated (autoimmune) causes, not in hereditary spherocytosis or G6PD deficiency.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. LDH is released from lysed RBCs (elevated), haptoglobin binds free haemoglobin and is consumed (reduced/absent), and a positive DAT indicates IgG or complement coating the RBC surface — the hallmark of autoimmune haemolysis.
